cards.text: Jeremiah, God's prophet, is still confined in the courtyard of the guard when the word of the LORD comes to him a second time. Locked up, stuck in one spot, waiting on somebody to open the door? Friend, I did YEARS of that in the back of a junk drawer.
God starts by saying who's talking: the LORD who made the earth, formed it and established it. When the One who MADE the planet opens with His résumé, you put your phone down and listen.

cards.question: Then God gives Jeremiah, stuck in that courtyard, an invitation. What does God tell him to do?
God promises that if Jeremiah calls, He'll show him things Jeremiah already knows.

cards.text: Now God speaks about Jerusalem itself. Houses, even the palaces of Judah's kings, have been torn down for defense against the siege ramps and the sword.

cards.question: God says the ___ are coming to fight Jerusalem and fill those torn-down places with the bodies of the men He strikes down.
God says He has hidden His face from Jerusalem. Why?

answers.text: Because its walls are too weak

cards.text: Heavy stuff. And then God says one word that flips the WHOLE thing around: Nevertheless. Friend, if my life story had one word on the cover, it'd be that one.

cards.question: After the anger and the hidden face, what does God say He'll bring to Jerusalem?
God says He'll restore Judah and Israel from captivity and rebuild them as in former times.
God says He'll cleanse His people from all the iniquity they've committed against Him and ___ all their sins of rebellion.

cards.text: And this is no quiet little fix. God says the city will bring Him renown, joy, praise and glory before ALL the nations of the earth.

cards.question: When the nations hear about all the good God does for Jerusalem, what do they do?

cards.text: Now God brings up what people say about this place: a wasteland, streets deserted, without man or beast. Friend, I know empty. I spent years in a junk drawer counting falling dust for FUN.

cards.question: What does God say will be heard again in those deserted streets of Jerusalem?
Among those happy sounds in the streets, God says there will be the voices of the ___ and the ___.
God says people will once again bring thank offerings into the house of the LORD.

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts talks about that same desolate place, without man or beast, and all its cities. Picture the emptiest, quietest spot you know. Now hold on to your apron.

cards.question: In that desolate place, what does God say there will be once more for shepherds?
God says the flocks will again pass under the hands of the one who counts them, but only inside Jerusalem.

cards.text: Behold, the days are coming, God says, when He'll fulfill the gracious promise He spoke to the house of Israel and the house of Judah. Friend, when God says "I will," it is NOT like me saying I'll clean the oven this weekend.

cards.question: In those days, God says He'll cause something to sprout for David, Israel's great king. What is it?
The righteous Branch God raises up for David will administer justice and righteousness in the land.

cards.text: In those days, Judah will be saved and Jerusalem will dwell securely. And the city gets a name. Not a nickname, friend. A NAME.

cards.question: God says the name Jerusalem will be called is The LORD Our ___.

cards.text: Then God makes two promises that go hand in hand. One is about David's throne, and one is about the priests who are Levites.

cards.question: God says there will be times when David has no man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel.
God says the priests who are Levites will never fail to have a man before Him. Doing what?

cards.text: The word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah again. This time God puts His promise right next to something that has never once missed a shift.

cards.question: God says His covenant with David could be broken only if someone could break His covenant with what?
By talking about day and night, God is saying His covenant with David and the Levites could break any day now.

cards.text: Nobody has ever stopped the morning. Friend, I've TRIED, every single day, with the snooze button, and nine minutes later morning is STILL standing there.

cards.question: God says He'll multiply the descendants of David and the Levites. He compares them to the hosts of heaven and to what else that can't be measured?

cards.text: The word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah once more. God asks if he's noticed what people are saying: that the LORD has rejected the two families He had chosen.

cards.question: Because of what they're saying, how do these people treat God's people?

answers.text: They no longer see them as a nation
They fear them as a nation

cards.text: So God answers with day and night again, plus the fixed order of heaven and earth: if He hadn't set those in place, then He'd reject the descendants of Jacob, father of Israel's tribes, and of David. Spoiler, friend: the sun came up this morning.

cards.question: God ends with this promise about the descendants of Jacob and David: He will restore them from captivity and have ___ on them.

findings.problem: The passage starts mid-thought: Jeremiah is 'still' confined, and the word comes 'a second time' (Jer 33:1). The opening card doesn't explain either one. It doesn't say why Jeremiah is confined or what is happening in Jerusalem, and it spends one of its three sentences on a joke.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Call to Me' is in God's first-person voice with a capitalized 'Me'. The wrong answers ('Wait in silence', 'Write it all down') aren't, so the right answer sounds more like the Bible and stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: For why God hid His face, the wrong answers 'Because its walls are too weak' and 'Because its people stopped singing' aren't believable reasons. The second one reads as silly, so 'Because of all its wickedness' is the obvious pick.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'Heavy stuff.', the 'Nevertheless' sentence, and the life-story joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'A new king and army' isn't clearly false across the passage. Later God promises a righteous Branch for David who administers justice (Jer 33:15) and a man on David's throne (Jer 33:17), so a baker could argue that a new king is part of what God brings.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The joke compares the deserted wasteland 'without man or beast' to the junk drawer. But the drawer wasn't empty. It was full of paper and dust and shared with friends (rubber bands, batteries, the key, the coupon). The core action, being deserted, doesn't match.

rule.text: 2. The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the wasteland sentence, 'Friend, I know empty.', and the drawer sentence.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The two-blank card asks the baker to put 'bride' and 'bridegroom' in an exact order. Nothing told earlier lets the baker reason out the order, and 'bridegroom' then 'bride' means the same thing. That tests unseen wording, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The song the people sing in Jer 33:11 is never told: 'Give thanks to the LORD of Hosts, for the LORD is good; His loving devotion endures forever.' It is a key line of the passage, and the walkthrough skips it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the LORD of Hosts sentence, 'Picture the emptiest, quietest spot you know.', and 'Now hold on to your apron.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Stop 2's choice cards open with the same type sequence as stop 1's: multiple choice, then true or false on the same verse, then fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This story card has 4 sentences: 'In those days...', 'And the city gets a name.', 'Not a nickname, friend.', and 'A NAME.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card comes after cards 10 and 11 have already covered Jer 33:20–21, and it goes back to cite Jer 33:20. It tells no new part of the passage. It is only a joke, so it's a recap. Its opening line 'Nobody has ever stopped the morning' is also stated as fact, and a baker could point to Joshua 10:13, where the sun stood still.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.
